blocks.text: The Zscaler service performs global time-ordered log consolidation, with potential latency ranging from several seconds to a few minutes, so you can view every transaction that your users perform regardless of where they are in the world.

Logs are stored for 180 days in the Zscaler Nanolog servers. Zscaler also offers the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS), a virtual machine (VM) that can stream web traffic logs in real time from the Zscaler Nanolog to your security information and event management (SIEM) system, such as Splunk, enabling real-time alerting, correlation with the logs of your firewall and other devices, and long-term local log archival. Contact the Zscaler Account team or Zscaler Support for more information on subscribing to NSS.
The Insights Logs pages provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: View logs for each transaction processed by Zscaler.
Quickly access the desired logs with the help of multiple filters and operators when troubleshooting.

blocks.text: Interactive reports support UTF-8 characters, enabling the display of special characters.
You can view logs for the following:

blocks.item: Web: View transactions initiated from any device (e.g., Windows, Mac, Mobile Devices, etc.). You can view the Page Risk Index score for each URL requested, the number of bytes sent and received, and more.
You can view the logs for messages that triggered the inline DLP rules in the Web Insights Logs for Webex.

Mobile: View transactions initiated from the browsers of mobile devices only. The logs appear based on the device OS. You can view the Page Risk Index score for each URL requested, the number of bytes sent and received, and more.
Firewall: View details such as the rule that was applied, the client and server details, and the network services and applications.
DNS: View data, such as the DNS request and response details.
Tunnel: View data about GRE and IPSec tunnels, such as their health, status, and authentication and encryption algorithms.
SaaS Security: View every scan performed by the Zscaler SaaS Connector of the data based on your SaaS application tenant.
Endpoint DLP: View activities specific to Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
Email DLP Insights: View insights into Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
Extranet: View insights into extranets.
Sandbox Verdict Insights: View Sandbox analysis logs.

blocks.text: Zscaler Support can view Tunnel Insights even if Remote Assistance is disabled.
On the Insights Logs pages (Logs> choose the Insights page you want to view logs for > Logs), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Clear all filters. You'll be directed back to the default Insights page.
Click to show or hide the left pane.
Choose a predefined time frame or select Custom to use the calendar and time menus to define your own time frame. In Custom, the end date can be up to 92 days after start date.

View the transactions in a log table. You can search for specific entries wherever you see a magnifying glass on a column field name. You can also sort certain columns by ascending or descending order. To customize the column fields:

Click the icon (#5) on the top right of the logs to list the available fields for display. Tick a box to add a column or clear it to remove a column. Alternatively, click Select all or Deselect all to display or remove all columns.
Drag a column to another location.
Resize a column by positioning the cursor on its border and dragging it to the desired width.
Customize your log view by selecting or deselecting which column fields you want to see. To view Insights Logs column fields for specific categories, see the following articles:
Web Insights Logs: Columns
Mobile Insights Logs: Columns
Firewall Insights Logs: Columns
DNS Insights Logs: Columns
Tunnel Insights Logs: Columns
Endpoint DLP Insights Logs: Columns
Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns
Extranet Insights Logs: Columns
Sandbox Verdict Insights Logs: Columns
Apply filters to narrow down the list or to find transactions, such as those associated with a specific user or URL.

blocks.text: Certain filters, like Users, Departments, Locations, and others, support the selection of multiple values. For these, you can select up to 200 values in a single filter. You can also choose to include or exclude the selected values. Also, certain filters support additional operators (i.e., Does Not Contain, Does Not Start With, Does Not End With, Is Null, Is Not Null) for filters that perform string match, like Threat Category and others.
To view Insights Logs filters for specific traffic types, see the following articles:

blocks.text: There are certain filter combinations that appear together in Insights Logs when applied, but won't appear together in Insights. For example, the Department and Location filters appear together in Insights Logs when applied, but won't appear together in Insights.

blocks.item: Select one of the following options:
Download: Download the list of transactions as a CSV file. You can export up to 1 million records with the available options of 100K, 250K, 500K, or 1 million records at a time.
Display: View the transactions stream on the screen as they are being retrieved from the storage. You can view up to 25K lines of data at a time with options from 1K, 5K, 10K, or 25K records.

You can continue to use the service while the export is in progress. The limit for the number of times you can export is 20 requests/hour. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.

blocks.text: For URL-based column values in the Logs display and CSV files, there is a character limit of 2,041 in the sub-URL string. For example, in www.zscaler.com/index.html, www.zscaler.com is the domain and /index.html is the sub-URL. If the sub-URL exceeds the 2,041 character limit, it is truncated. This does not affect the behavior or functionality of the URL.

blocks.item: Choose the number of records that you want displayed on the page.
Click Run Query to activate your changes.

If the query takes longer than 30 seconds, the Export to Background option becomes available. Selecting this option allows you to save the CSV file by providing a name and moving the query execution to the background. You can then monitor the query's progress in the Job Center, accessible via the Export button on the top right of the page. The CSV file is ready for download from the Job Center as soon as query execution is completed. The query continues to run in the background even if you navigate away from this page. You can monitor the execution progress, cancel the process, and download the CSV file from the Job Center. The report stops generating as soon as it reaches your selected record limit, even if more matching records are available.
The organization-wide limit for background query exports is 10, which includes all queries that are either completed or currently in progress.
Admins can export a single query to the background at a time, as long as the organization's maximum limit has not been reached.
An export in background query cannot be initiated by admins while another query is in progress.
Admins can run a foreground query even if a background query is currently running.

View the weblog time, which appears at the bottom of every window. The Nanolog servers collect the logs of all users worldwide, and then consolidate and correlate them. The weblog time displays the date and time of the logs that are being processed by the Nanolog servers.
Go to the Insights page.
Download the report that was run in the background from the Export list by clicking the Export button.
Reports are accessible for download or on-screen viewing for only 72 hours following the completion of execution.
